utterances.text: I am aware that under at least one iteration of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan as it was forwarded, parts of this area would be under the -- or it would be awarded to the Bosnian Muslim side, because at that time they represented the dominant population group there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the pre-war plan, Cutileiro's plan, that is to say, the Lisbon agreement that was accepted by Serbs, Muslims, and Croats alike, envisaged this area to become part of the Muslim constituent unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the Cutileiro Plan, so I cannot comment one way or another on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in this sector all the way up to March, April, 1993, until the proclamation of the protected area, there were 15- to 18.000 active combatants of the BH Army? The 8th Operative Group it used to be called, the 28th Division, and the 8th Operative Group alternatively.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In answer to your second question first, the 8th Operative Group ultimately becomes the 28th Infantry Division. So there are no -- they're not two separate units. It's one particular unit. I don't know that I've ever seen a number as high as 15- to 18.000 combatants associated with those units at the time, but -- and again, as you note, by the size of territory under their control, there was a sizable Bosnian Muslim military presence in that area that represented a significant threat to the VRS there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they posed a threat not only to the VRS but also to the Serbian civilians? And do you know that before the proclamation of the protected area they had killed over 1.300 Serbian civilians in this area that they controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the map can be enlarged again, this area that is marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can -- again, I don't know the number 1300 civilians, but I agree with your broad assertion that Bosnian Muslim forces did attack Serbian-held villages and Serbian civilians were casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you note what were the objectives of this military group in this sector in 1992 and 1993? Was it their aim to link up with Central Bosnia, with the 2nd Corps in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was ultimately the goal of the Muslim military forces at that time was to, in fact, establish a ground link with the 2nd Corps so there would be a continuous territory that was held by the Bosnian Muslim forces, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you analysed our military opponents at all, their intentions, their forces, their actions, in order to better understand the actions of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did to a limited degree look at the military operations carried out by, well, first OG8 and later the 28th Infantry Division, but I have to emphasise to a limited degree. There was a separate investigation team at the Office of the Prosecutor at the time who was investigating human rights allegations and war crimes allegations related to the military forces of the 28th Infantry Division, and Naser Oric specifically, against the Serbs in that particular area. So in that particular context, it was a separate investigation. They had separate military analysts who worked on that particular issue. So while I don't have details of that, I try to at least keep myself apprised enough to be able to put -- as you say, understand the history and the context of what had happened and how that may have played a role in what later happened in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that you noted in your report that Bratunac was reduced to a very small territory? And we can see that on this map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, particularly January and February of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll leave this document for a moment. Can we see 1D4027, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Butler, did you know that I had issued an appeal to the Muslim people that they should not fight, that their area would probably go to their constituent unit, and that they should just stay put and wait for a solution, for a peaceful solution?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to Eastern Bosnia; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I issued that during the fighting. It was meant in general terms, for all Muslims, but specifically for this populous there, because this area was meant to become Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a two-part question. The first part is, no, I'm not aware of that particular proclamation, and secondly, from my review of the military documents, I don't recall ever seeing a document which would any way reflect that the territory that the VRS was presently fighting on with respect to those areas in question were intended ultimately to fall back under Bosnian Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I note the time. So we'll take a break now, if it is convenient for you, for 20 minutes and resume at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Excellency, this document hasn't been translated yet, but I was not counting on using it in the first place. Can I please ask for it to be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out to you and let the interpreters check what I'm saying. This is a document dated the 1st of October, 1992. The staff, the District Staff of Tuzla is asking the Main Staff for different things. Number 1: "From the free territory of Bratunac, Zvornik, Srebrenica, and Vlasenica, a group of officers and soldiers managed to get to the District Staff of Tuzla in order to co-ordinate action and render assistance, namely, penetrating the corridor, sending personnel and resources for waging struggle, assisting in food and medicine for about 70.000 refugees."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note that the French booth is empty, and Judge Flavia Lattanzi does not get any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we proceed now? Oh. We'll wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Lattanzi kindly agreed to follow in English, so shall we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So for example, paragraph 4, I'll move on to that straight away. The commander of the staff of Bratunac is saying the following, the second sentence: "Since the beginning the war we have held a large part of the territory of our municipalities and no Chetnik has ever arrived in our territory and no Chetnik foot will ever step on our soil." As you know, they called all Serbs Chetniks; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that is a derogatory term that Muslims would address Serbs as, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at the penultimate sentence. It says: "In Tuzla we have a few units that have completed their training and are awaiting mobilisation. Right now in that area, there are large-scale attacks, and we have many casualties and many wounded, especially in the area around Zvornik, Snagovo, Kamenica, and Novo Selo. Could something please be done with the convoy of humanitarian aid. Could it be sent to this territory." So on the 1st of October there was fighting in that area. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, I can't give you a specific date, but I agree with your assertion that at this point in time, particularly October/November, that the Bosnian Muslim military forces do control a rather large swathe of the area that we've previously described as the upper Podrinje area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2331, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We're looking for other ones, too, but, well, basically you accept that they held this under their control. Can we please go back to the map, 1D4888.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, Mr. Butler, according to your findings what was the objective of the Muslim part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? What was the objective of the HVO? And what was the objective of the Army of Republika Srpska? Or let me help you with all of this. Did the HVO aspire to control all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and did the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina aspire for control over all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the question relating to the HVO, I did absolutely no research related to the HVO, so I cannot comment with any authority as to what their war aims were. With respect to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the government in Sarajevo of Bosnia and Herzegovina viewed themselves as the legitimate government of the entire country of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so ultimately the war aim of the army of the -- Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to, to the degree that they could, seek their political leadership's control over all of that territory. You know, at the beginning their primary missions were to defend the territory that they had relative to the beginning part of the war, but ultimately one would say that the goal of the Army of the Republika Srpska [sic] was to reassert the authority of the government in Sarajevo over the entire country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood this properly. Did you say that the aim of the Army of Republika Srpska was to establish the authority of the Sarajevo government throughout the territory or what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see your point, and I clearly misspoke. The goal of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to establish their control over the entirety of Bosnia and Herzegovina as the military arm of the government in Sarajevo. If I said "Republika Srpska," I certainly didn't mean to in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to the six strategic objectives that you mention, although they're not from 1995 and not from Podrinje only. However, do you agree that the Army of Republika Srpska did not have as its aim exercising control over all of Bosnia and Herzegovina as opposed to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree that the Serb side, as far as this enclave is concerned, it tolerated it until the spring of 1993? That is to say, they did not take any measures or did not conduct any operations to resolve that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, the phrase that's translated in English is "as far as this enclave is concerned." Are you referring to again the map where you're talking about the territory under the control of the Bosnia-Herzegovina military forces at this time, or are you referring to one of the UN enclaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought that you had the same thing on your screen as I do. The map that we saw a few moments ago from Zvornik to -- to the Drina to Zepa --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown this in e-court. Could something be done with e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have this map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this map, sir, yes. It's just the phrase that you used, "enclave," threw me off and that was how it was translated in English. I -- so I just wanted to be clear exactly what we were talking about. I would disagree with your comment. The answer that I come to based on the military documents is that beginning in late December and continuing through January and February and March of 1993, specifically the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the Birac Infantry Brigade, and elements of the Milici and Vlasenica Infantry Brigades engaged in military operations which ultimately reduced the size of the Bosnian-Muslim-held territory by at least a third, their primary objective being to capture and control the Cerska region. So given what was occurring in that part of the area at the time, no, sir, I can't agree that there were no measures taken by the VRS to resolve the enemy situation as it existed. I believe they were very active during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you the following: Let us be very precise with our wording. This is what I'm asking you: Before the spring of 1991 -- no, 1993, did the Army of Republika Srpska conduct an operation? I'm not talking about actions. I'm not talking about fighting. Conducted by a single brigade, a single battalion, two brigades, parts of a single corps. I hope that you make a distinction between a military operation and a skirmish or a military action. Were there any military operations aimed at liberating this area before the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just for the record, the previous question that

utterances.speaker: MR. BUTLER ANSWERED WAS
utterances.text: "Thank you. And do you agree that the Serb side, as far as this enclave is concerned, it tolerated it until the spring of 1993? That is to say that they did not take any measures or did not conduct any operations to resolve that."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The point is operations. There were clashes on a daily basis throughout Bosnia, but do you agree, Mr. Butler, that an operation is a planned activity of a strategic formation of the military, not of two brigades?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree with your definition. My definition of an operation-level activity would raise to a multi-brigade operation within a single corps. If I were to accept your definition, which would appear to be larger, that an operation had to at least involve multiple corps-level organisations, you would exclude a lot of military activity under that to include Krivaja 95, which was again a multi-brigade military operation conducted by a single corps. Hence why I don't agree with your definition as to what an operation is. I believe that, again, multi-brigade military operations meet that definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we agree that the Army of Republika Srpska took more comprehensive action only in the spring of 1993 and liberated this area with the exception of Srebrenica and Zepa in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In fact, given the severity of the winter conditions in January and February of 1993 particularly, conditions so severe that there were humanitarian food drops by various national groups related to Bosnia to try and parachute food in there, there was only so much that you could do during that period because of the adverse weather conditions, but once the spring started and the weather conditions improved and the roads became far more passable, the scale of military operations increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I hope that you believe that it was winter-time for the Muslims, too, and that there was snow for them as well, and that did not prevent them from attacking us all the time; right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, correct, sir, in the sense that military operations were not suspended by either side during the winter conditions. The winter conditions just impacted the ability of both sides to really conduct wide-ranging military operations, but the war didn't stop.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, can we have this map admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you ask any question about this map to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I put a question about the zone that was controlled by the Muslim army in January 1993, and the witness said that that corresponds to his knowledge, namely that this zone was under the control of the 8th Operative Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2232, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Butler, that it was I who stopped our army on the outskirts of Srebrenica, and I even prohibited war crime investigations in order to stop vengeful behaviour on the part of the Serbs who were in the army and who hailed from that area? Did you come across any such document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whose order it was to stop military operations. If General Mladic gave the order, then I assume that he did so under your authority, so again if it turns out that it ultimately was your order to do that and he followed that, it certainly wouldn't surprise me. I am not aware of an order that you have given that prohibited Bosnian Serb military or police forces from conducting war crimes investigations in that particular area for any reason, so -- again, I'm not -- I don't recall ever seeing a document that reflects that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we have enough time, we're going to show you that document. It's already been admitted. All right. Did you know that we had agreed to have Srebrenica and Zepa declared safe havens and that that was supposed to be done on the basis of a bilateral agreement signed by Mladic and Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, I understand that General Mladic and General Halilovic did sign a bilateral agreement. I know I've probably put this material in my report, but I can't recall at this particular instant where that fell chronologically in time with the creation of the safe area, whether it was before or after, sir. I just don't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are certainly familiar with the terms "a demilitarised area" and "an undefended area," right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I think the sense where I think you're going with this question, I do understand the terms as they're used with relation to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a mistranslation. The right word would be "non-defended" for "undefended." "Non-defended" would be right. [In English] Would be probably non-defended or -- non-defended are one kind and another kind is demilitarised. [Interpretation] Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I understand -- I understand there are differences between a non-defended area and a demilitarised in that sense. Again, the creation of the United Nations safe area related to Srebrenica had provisions for it being demilitarised. So again I understand the terminology is where I think you're going to go with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you share your understanding with us so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this is going where I believe it is, I mean the question is going to be whether or not my opinion is whether or not Srebrenica was demilitarised in the sense of the agreements as seen by both the UN and the bilateral agreement with Mladic and General Halilovic, and I've testified about that kind of issue before, so I believe that's where he's going with this, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell us the difference between demilitarisation and non-defence, as far as you understand them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are provisions - and again I'm not an expert in this field - under international law where certain areas can be declared open cities or open areas. For example, one comes to mind is during World War II the retreat of the American army through the -- Manila, the city of Manila, and it was declared -- after the army had passed through it and had no intentions of defending, it was declared an open city in order that the attacking Japanese military forces would know that it was a completely undefended area and that they did not have to engage in military operations endangering the civilian population. That is my understanding in broad context of the difference between a demilitarised and open or undefended areas.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5546. Could we that called up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Butler, do you agree that an undefended area and a demilitarised area are agreed upon between the parties in conflict according to Protocol I -- Additional Protocol I. Article 59 as far as undefended areas are concerned, and Article 60 pertains to demilitarised zones. So that's the Additional Protocols.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm aware that generally they are based on bilateral agreements between the various warring parties. They can, of course, be brokered by a third party, or in the case where the ICRC always functions as a neutral party in this case. But, yeah, customarily when two combatants are fighting, those are the type of things that they would negotiate for whatever their purposes are.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 37 in Serbian and page 22 in English. One page earlier in Serbian to see what the undefended place is. Page 36 in Serbian. Probably one page earlier in English. Oh, no. The English page can stay. [In English] Non-defended localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please see what it says. The competent authorities of the warring party may proclaim as non-defended any area where conflicting parties are in contact, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the conditions that have to be met. Page 4. "The declaration made under paragraph 2 shall be addressed to the adverse party and shall define and describe as precisely as possible the limits of the non-defended locality. The party to the conflict which the declaration is addressed shall acknowledge its receipt and shall treat the locality as a non-defended locality." And 5: "The parties of the conflict may agree on the establishment of non-defended localities do not fulfil the conditions laid down in paragraph 2. The agreement should define the methods of supervision." And number 7: "A locality loses its status as a non-defended locality when it ceases to fulfil the conditions laid down in paragraph 2 ..." Et cetera. Do you know of any place in Bosnia-Herzegovina which had the status of a non-defended locality?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge in this particular context. There may be, but none of them are coming to mind to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now put to you the position of the Defence. The Muslim side declared war on the Serbian side, and in doing so did not require us to recognise any locality as undefended or non-defended; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again going back to prior testimony on this, I mean, I don't know that I would be the appropriate authority to make a determination as to which side declared war on which side, and I don't know that I can answer the second part of your question about a declaration of war not requiring, you say "us," but any side to recognise any locality as undefended or non-defended. I just don't know that I can answer that question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm telling you that they declared war on us on the 20th of June, and we asked that it be annulled throughout that year to make the conflict last shorter. Now I'm asking you, when somebody wants war and does not ask for any place to be recognised as non-defended, then what could that side expect except to have a war?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would answer that with respect to the laws as they apply to armed conflict. Absent a specific designation of what would be a non-defended area, a warring party, without having information or without being notified that it was an undefended area, a warring party would have a legitimate right to conduct military operations in that area. Again, I caveat that with the fact that all of the other rules related to the protection of civilians and civilian objects and protected personnel are still applicable, but I -- I agree with your point that if we're talking about Article 59, absent a specific designation, one side, you know, could assume that the territory that they are attacking is, in fact, defended by their adversary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see paragraph -- that is to say Article 60, both Serbian and English. In English it would be the bottom of the page, and in Serbian too. Article 60 relates to demilitarised zones and it says, doesn't it: "It is prohibited for the parties to the conflict to extend their military operations to zones on which they have confirmed by agreement the status of demilitarised zone ..." And then paragraph 2. If we could turn to the next page in English. "The agreement shall be an express agreement, may be concluded verbally or in writing, either directly or through a Protecting Power or any impartial humanitarian organisation ..." Now, may I draw your attention to paragraph 3 where the conditions that a demilitarised zone must meet are listed. "All combatants as well as mobile and immobile military equipment must be evacuated. "No hostile use shall be made of fixed military installations. "No acts of hostility be shall committed by the authorities or by the population ... "Any activity linked to the military effort must have ceased." And in paragraph 5: "The Party which is in control of such a zone shall mark it, so far as possible, by such signs as may be agreed upon with the other Party, which shall be displayed where they are clearly visible, especially on its perimeter and limits and on highways." And paragraph 6: "If the fighting draws near to a demilitarised zone, and if the Parties to the conflict have so agreed, none of them may use the zone for purposes related to the conduct of military operations or unilaterally revoke its status." "7. If one the parties to the conflict commits a material breach of the provisions of paragraphs 3 or 6, the other party shall be released from its obligations under the agreement conferring upon the zone the status of demilitarised zone. In such an eventuality, the zone loses its status but shall continue to enjoy the protection provided by the other provisions ..." et cetera, et cetera. We have seen that there were no non-defended places. Do you know of any demilitarised place in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in the sense that particularly beginning in April and May of 1993 in Eastern Bosnia, the United Nations designated Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde as demilitarised zones. So believe again I don't know the specific dates and times because I think there were two separate UN Resolutions related to those, but they are in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection. Sorry to interrupt, but just for precision and to help me, could I know what document - there's been quite a lot of discussion about it - Mr. Karadzic was referring to at line -- at page 10, line 1 today, the document he says where the Muslim side on 22nd of June declared war against Serbia, Montenegro, and the Serbian autonomous regions in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect to Mr. Nicholls, when the Muslim side provides the original documents to us, we will provide them to you, but this is common knowledge in our public. This is a mutilated transcript of one of their sessions. We'll show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Butler, Caligula proclaimed his horse to be a senator although he was certainly not a senator. Were these zones really demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can't comment on the status of Caligula, but I have testified previously that based on my knowledge of the activities that occurred after the creation of the safe areas as they were labelled by the UN, they were not in fact truly demilitarised. And I believe I've been fairly consistent with my testimony through the years that first OG8 and later, as it was redesignated, the 28th Infantry Division of 2 Corps did conduct military operations out of both the Srebrenica and Zepa safe areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your information. I'd like to show you the document by virtue of which I stopped the operation in 1993. D0043.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender at least these two Articles, although I believe international covenants should be admitted en bloc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's necessary for us to admit the laws. What do you think, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, it's up to the Chamber. You can already refer to these laws, and we can refer to them as well without them being admitted, so whatever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I agree. I don't think they need to be admitted. I don't think there's going to be a dispute about what the provisions of these Articles say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Absolutely. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we don't have to have it admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the English version, 16 April 1993. "I hereby order: "1. Cease all operations of the Army of Republika Srpska against Srebrenica and its surroundings, except for those of necessary defence. "2. Stop the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska at the positions reached and prevent their entry into Srebrenica. "3. Facilitate the passage of all humanitarian convoys both entering and leaving Srebrenica. "4. Ensure pacification of the town in such a way that Muslim forces surrender weapons to UNPROFOR, who will then store them on a two-key basis jointly with the Serbian forces. "5. After the surrender of weapons, all the Muslim soldiers shall be treated like all other civilians. "Provide protection for all civilians and give them the liberty to choose between leaving and staying. "6. Do not conduct any investigations into war crimes until the situation around Srebrenica is settled. "7. Carry the order out immediately and fully inform me thereof." Did you have insight into this document, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe I've testified before on this. I was not aware of this document. I've not seen this document until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that combatants are hereby considered as civilians from the moment when they surrender their weapons not to us but to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that is your provision as written in paragraph 5, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you add anything to this? Could I have added anything to this order to make life in Srebrenica easier? Protection of civilians and respect for civilians is provided for. Amnesty of the fighters, assistance to humanitarian organisations.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Respectfully, sir, I don't know that my opinion on what you should or should not have put in a particular presidential decree assists the Trial Chamber, and I don't know that -- you know, I'm not a head of state. I don't know that I would have the relevant expertise to be able to comment as to the appropriateness of a presidential decree of this nature. You put in this document what you put in this document for your reasons, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Butler, do we agree that in those international documents and in our bilateral agreement, the boundaries of these two protected areas are defined and marked on the map and in the agreement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure I can agree with that comment because I am aware of military documents which in some cases they're actually United Nations documents where General Zivanovic is informing the Dutch Battalion commander in, I believe, January of 1995, that it is his opinion, presumably representing the VRS, that to that date, the actual boundaries of the Srebrenica safe area have never been probably demarcated between the VRS side and the -- the Bosnian Muslim side within the enclave. So again while they may be on a map and things of that nature, it is my understanding that even through 1995, the Army of the Republika Srpska military leadership there did not believe that the safe area was properly demarcated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, if you say the task of the VRS was to reduce the enclave to the narrow urban area, then you should know that there existed agreed and signed boundaries of that area that the Muslim side did not honour. Instead, they expanded the area to the detriment of the Serbs. Were these two protected areas or one? Because they were drawn as two.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, I don't know the answer to that in that sense. What I can reiterate is that I know that General Zivanovic raised the issue of the proper demarcation of the enclave in January of 1995, and I believe that at some point in March of 1995, General Smith had the occasion to meet with VRS officers, I believe General Zivanovic again, at Vlasenica and the Drina Corps, and if I recall correctly, General Smith was at that point also presented with a map which indicated where the VRS believed that the actual boundaries of the enclave should be demarcated as.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Butler, you are evaluating operations around Srebrenica. Among other things, account should be taken of legality and lawfulness. I'm asking you whether that belt together with the road between Srebrenica and Zepa fell under Serbian control under the agreement, and did the Muslim side violate that? Did you see that agreement and the map when you were making your expert report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. And again, with respect to your specific question, I don't know the answer, and more so, it was not relevant to the analysis that I was doing. The analysis that I was performing with respect to the operations around Srebrenica did not deal with the question of whether or not the VRS's attack into the enclave per se was lawful or not. Certainly I'm not a person who can give the Court any expert opinion as to whether attacking a UN safe area is or is not a crime. My position is that, and again I've testified to this before, is that given the fact that the ABiH military forces in the enclave were armed and did conduct military operations out of the enclave, that the VRS had a legitimate right to engage in military operations against the 28th Infantry Division there. That's not a legal finding. That's, in my sense, a military finding. I believe they had that right because it was an armed combatant that they were facing. So given that that was my starting point of my analysis, where the actual boundary of the enclave was and who controlled what particular territory was not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree, and you called it as a new task or a follow-up task, do you agree that the task that the VRS had was an action, not an operation, and it was called "action" in the documents, and this action was to separate Srebrenica from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can answer this with a yes or no. You wrote that in your report.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, I don't believe that, and in fact, you know, it's an operation; and secondly, if it's the exact language of the operations order, this is why I referenced the Krivaja 95 operations order in my reports. The language speaks for itself in that particular order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe the language is this: "Order for active combat actions," not operations. And for forensic purposes, this is a very important distinction. "Order for combat action."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D35. We don't need the Serbian. This is the agreement. We should go to the last page where the map is. Demilitarised zone. Any combat operation is directly prohibited by Article 60 of the Protocol I and Additional Protocols of the Geneva Conventions. We can leaf through this but we don't have much time so that the witness can see the map. Then it must be the addendum or perhaps the penultimate page. No. Obviously, the map is not part of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll look for it, and we'll show it to you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Before we adjourn, do you remember the exact name of that Krivaja order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not off the top of my head, sir. I mean the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's -- I don't want to interrupt. It's P04481. I mean, I think it would be much simpler just to bring up Krivaja 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give the number again, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must be a translation, but I'll read it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do we agree that this was not envisaged as an operation, just combat activities with the limited task. "OP number" means operative number, not number of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you assist us, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I -- I guess it's a linguistic issue between -- as I've testified, between what I consider an operation and what Mr. Karadzic considers an operation. Again from my perspective, that's the beauty about military orders. It means what it says and it says what it means for clarity's sake. Whether or not it's a -- a combat action or whether it's an operation and what that means certainly doesn't change my view of what the Krivaja 95 order is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I see what deceived you. OP 1 is the operative number of the document, number one in the set of documents expected during this action. This abbreviation OP means operative number. This is the first document in a series expected to follow from this action. Do you now understand that this was not conceived or called an operation, but I understand the translation put you on the wrong track.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're just going to have to agree to disagree on that particular terminology issue, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Excellency, what's the situation with time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 20th day of April, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.31 p.m.,
